definitions.transformer: True-row expected loss with identified copying head removed minus intact-network loss, on identical observed sequences.
definitions.bayes: Known-uniform expected loss minus saved informed Bayesian predictive loss. This is a different baseline from the disabled transformer.
definitions.control: True-row expected loss with independently selected comparison head removed minus intact-network loss.
definitions.transformer_vs_uniform: Known-uniform expected loss minus intact-transformer expected loss; matches the Bayesian comparison baseline.
definitions.disabled_vs_uniform: Disabled-transformer expected loss minus known-uniform expected loss; directly measures the baseline discrepancy.
definitions.first_positive: Earliest saved time whose mean benefit exceeds numerical zero; early isolated positive points may precede the eventual crossing.
definitions.final_positive_run: First time of the final strictly positive run through time 1024; right-censored if the last value is nonpositive. It is not a claim of positivity beyond 1024.
definitions.expectation: At each observed sequence, average next-token log loss over its true transition row; then average over independent sequences conditional on source depth.
definitions.cumulative: Sum of those paired expected next-token loss differences from t=1 through n; first token supplied free.

uncertainty.resampling: Whole source sequences, independently within each depth, paired across all times and predictors.
uncertainty.curve_intervals: Pointwise 95% Student-t intervals; not simultaneous bands.
uncertainty.crossing_intervals: 2.5%, 50%, 97.5% order statistics across all bootstrap draws. Right-censored crossings retained as infinity (JSON null for a censored quantile); finite-only intervals are not reported.
uncertainty.caution: Last crossings of unsmoothed empirical means are sensitive to late fluctuations. Bootstrap intervals are exploratory, particularly if multiple crossings or censoring occur.

selection: Depth one is highlighted after reviewing existing results because it has delayed payoff; all nine depths and the comparison-head intervention remain in the appendix data.
limitations: The ablated transformer has not been identified with the original adaptive LSA unigram.
The intact transformer and informed Bayes are not pure copier components.
Agreement between these two payoff times is therefore an empirical comparison, not a direct test of the archived pure-unigram/pure-copier crossing formula.
A causal effect of deleting this path need not equal an additive component weight.
Two source-selected finite paths, not all possible count profiles.
Wider bounds and a half-cell phase shift test the quadrature; all grids share the same sealed table approximation.
This validates the Bayes/source numerics, not transformer behavior or a causal timing conclusion.
